The operating point is a clinical trade-off, not a tuned hyperparameter. Reference burden: a retrospective ICU cohort reports a median 119 alarms/patient/day, ~5/hour (Sci Rep 2022, s41598-022-26261-4), and states that no threshold defining a 'high' alarm rate exists. The default is therefore justified as roughly doubling the existing burden, not as sitting under a published safe limit. Tuned on round-1 data — re-validate on round 2 without touching it.

## Caveats that must appear alongside any of the above

1. The +/- on the file-level accuracy is estimator seed variation on a handful of borderline files, NOT sampling uncertainty. Quote the Wilson or bootstrap CI instead.
2. File-level majority vote depends on clip length: re-voting the same events padded to the round-2 SOP length of 60-120 s takes pull recall to 0.000 while episode detection stays at 1.000. Report episode-level metrics.
3. No anomaly file reaches the <= 25,000 count detachment spec (KES 2025 s2.1); deepest is 27,251 (12.5 pF below the 28,000 count resting value). THE CRITERION IS UNREACHABLE ON THIS SENSOR, so this is not a fixation problem: it asks for a 50.1 pF drop out of an attached patch of about 30.0 pF, and even at zero capacitance the reading floors at 26,204 counts, 1,204 short. One of BASELINE_COUNTS, COUNTS_PER_PF or SPEC_DETACH_MAX is wrong; settle it with the author of s2.1 rather than with a stronger pump. Detection does not use this criterion - it gates on the delta from the tracked baseline.
4. LOOP 5 IMU signals are synthetic. No fusion number belongs in a results table.
5. Small classes: 0: Baseline n=5, 2: Peel n=10. A perfect 5/5 on the smallest of them carries a 95% CI of about 0.57-1.00, so it is not evidence of 100% performance.
6. Horizontal detachment produces NO lift signal on this patch. Measured over the round-1 corpus, Horizontal Pull recordings reach a median deepest delta of only -64 counts (deepest -161) and 0 of 10 cross the -300 lift gate - quieter than Friction, which is a normal class. What moves on those recordings is the positive/contact side (median max +456), so any Horizontal Pull the system does flag, it flags as a press-like event and not as detachment. Vertical Pull and Peel do cross the gate (10/10 each). Do not describe this device as detecting detachment in general until a horizontal-pull signal has been demonstrated.
7. All 81 recordings use Sensor-* columns, read as physical pad order without applying PAD_ORDER. That is no longer an assumption: the 1-by-1 press sweep in Press/1_by_1.csv peaks in strictly increasing column order (Spearman rho 1.0000, 0 inversions), so Sensor-N == physical pad N for this corpus. Re-run `python main.py --verify-pads` after any firmware or logger change. Still open, and it is now an open question in BOTH directions: the live sockets (?source=serial and ?source=client) default to permute=0, so they do NOT apply PAD_ORDER unless a caller passes &permute=1, and no 1-by-1 sweep has been captured through either. The setting in force is reported in the socket's own `started` message as `pad_order_applied`. Until that sweep exists, spatial output from LIVE hardware (heatmap, peel heading) is unverified whichever way the flag is set.
8. Single sensor mounting (1 session). Nothing here shows generalisation to a re-attached patch.
